channel.title: Tutorials on DATATWEETS
channel.description: Recent content in Tutorials on DATATWEETS

item.title: Build an AI Chatbot in Python: A Command-Line LLM Client
item.description: A from-scratch walkthrough of the pattern behind every LLM chatbot: one function that sends a message plus conversation history to a chat-completion API, a persona set by a system prompt, and a loop that keeps the conversation going.

item.title: The Single Responsibility Principle: One Class, One Reason to Change
item.description: The Single Responsibility Principle says a class should have only one reason to change. See it in action: take a Python AuthService that also owns its logging, find why that’s a problem, and refactor it into clean, focused classes.

item.title: How to Audit Multi-Agent Research Evidence Coverage in Python
item.description: Build an offline evidence gate for saved multi-agent findings. Define required and critical research facets, reject findings with unusable source records, measure breadth without rewarding repeated coverage, and send incomplete cases back for focused research.

item.title: How to Explain Scikit-Learn Predictions in a FastAPI API
item.description: Build a FastAPI regression endpoint that returns an inspectable baseline and per-feature effects for a linear scikit-learn pipeline. Train on original synthetic data, load one trusted artifact, and test that every displayed explanation reconstructs its prediction.

item.title: How to Rebuild a Python ML Environment from a Conda File
item.description: Create a clear environment.yml from direct machine learning dependencies, rebuild it under a second name, and verify the result with a hashed synthetic dataset, an executed scikit-learn workload, and a generated chart.

item.title: How to Use XGBoost Early Stopping Without Test Data Leakage
item.description: A beginner-friendly XGBoost regression workflow that gives training, validation, and test rows separate jobs, selects the number of trees with validation MAE, reads the zero-based best iteration correctly, and compares the locked model with useful baselines.

item.title: Logistic Regression vs. Random Forest for Heart Disease Prediction in Python
item.description: This project tutorial pits a scaled logistic regression model against a random forest on the real Cleveland heart disease dataset, shows how a single train/test split can flip the apparent winner, then settles it with 5-fold cross-validation, a recall-based tie-break, and one honest confirmation on held-out test data.

item.title: Python range(): How It Works and What It's Good for Beyond Loops
item.description: range() looks like it builds a list of numbers, but it doesn’t — it stores three integers and computes values on demand. This post covers what that means for memory and speed, how to index, slice, and reverse a range directly, and a reusable batching pattern built on its step argument, all verified against real Python 3.13 output.

item.title: How to Audit Attention Weights with Token Occlusion in Python
item.description: A beginner-friendly audit of one transparent attention-pooling calculation. Compare raw weights with signed classifier contributions, remove each token and rerun the model, and learn which conclusions an attention heatmap cannot support by itself.

item.title: How to Build a Testable AI Agent System Prompt in Python
item.description: Turn a fictional equipment-loan assistant’s decisions into a validated policy table, compile those rules into one provider-neutral system prompt, cover every policy with small scenarios, and test controlled JSON outputs without claiming live-model performance.
